Required fields per agent-passport SPEC.md Sec 4.1: schema (leave exactly as-is), id, owner. Everything else here is optional - delete what you don't need.

id must match agent://<lowercase-trust-domain>/<path>, e.g. agent://acme-bank.example/support/tier1-bot (SPEC.md Sec 3.1). The trust domain and path segments are validated lowercase-only - keep them lowercase even if the rest of your org's naming uses mixed case.

filesystem and models are DECLARATIONS OF INTENT for audit and inventory, not enforced controls - nothing in the stack grants or restricts access based on them today. See passport-templates/README.md in this catalog.
Remove every "//" key like this one before using this file as a real Agent Passport - they exist only to guide you while editing the template.
display_name: CHANGE ME: e.g. Tier-1 support triage bot (LangGraph)

attestation.//: method is one of: none, oidc, spiffe-svid, enclave-key, mtls-cert. spiffe-svid is shown here since LangGraph agents are commonly run behind a SPIRE-issued workload identity - use "none" instead if you don't have real attestation wired up yet. "none" is honest and legal; Idryx is meant to surface that gap as a finding, not have you fake a method to hide it.

filesystem.//: where this agent writes its own output

models.//: pin the exact model this graph's LLM node calls, so an auditor can compare declared vs. observed use
